repoAudit.httpsKeyIgnored.title: SSH key will not apply on this remote
repoAudit.httpsKeyIgnored.body: This project's origin is HTTPS, so git push/pull will use git-credential (HTTPS uses account + password / token), and the sshCommand entry written by NiceSSH will be ignored. To make this SSH key take effect: (1) add the matching public key on your git host (GitHub / GitLab / Gitee ...), then (2) in a terminal run git remote set-url origin git@...:user/repo.git, then (3) come back and rebind the identity.

httpsBindConfirm.title: SSH key will not apply on this remote
httpsBindConfirm.heading: {{project}} uses a {{protocol}} remote.
httpsBindConfirm.body1: NiceSSH will only swap the [user] block (user.name, user.email). Anything written under [core] sshCommand is **ignored** here — this remote uses account + password (or token) authentication, not SSH.
httpsBindConfirm.body2:
If you want this SSH key to take effect:
1) Add the matching public key on your git host.
2) Switch this project's remote to an SSH URL.
3) Then come back and bind the identity again.
